nodes.name: On New Email (IMAP)
nodes.notes: Watches the IMAP inbox and emits new emails as items (subject, body, attachments). Credential: IMAP credentials. IMAP host, port, user and password from your mail provider.

nodes.name: Prepare Approval Packet
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes requestId, summary, requestedBy. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Request Approval via Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Hold for Decision
nodes.notes: Pauses the execution until the resume webhook is called — this is the approval/HITL gate. Watch out: Long waits survive restarts, but the resume URL is single-use.

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.body?.decision || $json.decision }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Apply Approved Change (Airtable)
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Invoices' table, matched on invoiceId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Record Decline + Notify Requester
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Join Decision Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Track receipts: Telegram

**Pattern:** Expense Tracking · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Email

## Overview

Runs when mail lands in the inbox, and covers expenses work end to end across Telegram and Airtable.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. On New Email (IMAP)
2. Prepare Approval Packet
3. Request Approval via Telegram
4. Hold for Decision
5. Approved?
6. Apply Approved Change (Airtable)
7. Record Decline + Notify Requester
8. Join Decision Paths
9. Send Summary to Telegram

## Why it exists

Doing expenses work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On New Email (IMAP) → Prepare Approval Packet → Request Approval via Telegram → Hold for Decision → Approved? → Apply Approved Change (Airtable) → Record Decline + Notify Requester → Join Decision Paths → Send Summary to Telegram

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Airtable aligned by hand for expenses
- Expenses sequences that run over days and must survive a restart before Telegram
- Expenses work where "Prepare Approval Packet" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Expenses work that only reaches Telegram when mail lands in the inbox, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Airtable in step for expenses, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Telegram or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this expenses build
- Branches rejoin before Telegram, so a expenses run reports once rather than 9 times
- The pause before Telegram is durable — a expenses run survives a restart
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for expenses before wiring Telegram

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; IMAP credentials; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The workflow pauses on a Wait node configured to resume via webhook — n8n's actual human-in-the-loop primitive, not a polling loop. The resume URL is embedded directly in the approval message so approving is one click, and the paused execution burns no compute for however long the decision takes.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a timeout to the Wait node so unanswered approvals auto-decline after N hours.
2. Change the approval channel and confirm the resume link still works.
3. Add a third outcome (e.g. 'needs changes') alongside approve/decline.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**IMAP credentials**
IMAP host, port, user and password from your mail provider.
_Gotcha:_ Gmail requires an App Password and IMAP enabled in settings.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🙋 Human in the loop

The workflow pauses at the Wait node until a human posts a decision to the resume URL (included in the approval message). Approve → the action executes; anything else → recorded as declined. No timeout is set by default — add one under the Wait node's options if approvals go stale.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your expenses process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole expenses payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
